rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says thirst, cold, illness, and grief can alter someone; an unattributed line uses the verb of grief changing a person.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: (لاحه العطش ولوحه إذا غيره، والتاح إذا عطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed line uses laḥa for being changed, saying grief for a dead child, brother, or father had not changed the woman.
rows.anchor: ولم يلحها حزن على ابنم ... ولا أخ ولا أب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses lawwāḥa as changing and cites a line about scorching summer winds altering the speaker’s cousin.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: {لواحه} مغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bashar is the plural of bashara, meaning skin.
rows.anchor: والبشر: جمع بشرة، وهي الجلد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Fire blackens the skin of whoever is cast into it.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني تسود بشرة من يطرح فيها

rows.speaker: أبو رزين
rows.claim: Abu Razin says its blast sears the skin and leaves it blacker than night.
rows.anchor: وقال [أبو رزين] (¬10): يلفح الجلد لفحة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets the phrase as burning the skin.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني حراقة (¬2) الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says “burning the skin” conveys the effect rather than a full tafsir: fire pierces and alters the skin until it blackens.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: محرقة للجلد (¬4) -وهو معنى، وليس بتفسير-

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that it is visible to its inhabitants from five hundred years away.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يلوح لأهلها من مسيرة خمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: الحسن، ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Hasan and Ibn Kaysan also hold that it shines to its inhabitants from five hundred years away.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن (¬6)، وابن كيسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading lawwāḥa means shining like lightning, and al-bashar means people rather than skins.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد بها الجلود، وإنما معناها الناس

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes identify the nineteen as the Fire’s angelic keepers: Malik and eighteen others, fearsome in appearance, without mercy, and able to throw seventy thousand people where they choose.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: يقول على النار تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, Abu Jahl mocked that Muhammad had only nineteen helpers and challenged whether each hundred Quraysh could not overpower one.
rows.anchor: قالوا (¬7): ولما نزلت هذه الآية، قال اللعين أبو جهل

rows.speaker: أبو الأشدين
rows.claim: Abu al-Ashaddayn, a man of Banu Jumah, boasted that on the bridge he would push ten keepers with one shoulder and nine with the other, then enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الأشدين (¬3) -وهو رجل من بني جمح

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the angels are the Fire’s keepers; Muslims described them as jailers, and ḥaddād means a jailer who confines people.
rows.anchor: قال (أبو بكر) (¬7) بن الأنباري: لما أنزل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term ḥaddād means a jailer; the angels are keepers of the Fire.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: عس (¬1) الملائكة إلى السجانين من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that no one can endure or overcome the angels.
rows.anchor: "إلا ملائكة" أي: فمن يطيق الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their count is small; Muqatil glosses it as their fewness.
rows.anchor: أي: عددهم في القلة، وقال مقاتل: قلتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the number was a trial that led the disbelievers astray into making their taunts.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ضلاله لهم حتى قالوا ما قالوا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq interprets fitna as a test, since some claimed they could handle the keepers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي محنة؛ لأن بعضهم قال: أنا أكفي هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the number a trial so disbelievers would expose the denial within them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: جعلنا هذه العدة محنة لهم؟ ليظهروا ما عندهم من التكذيب

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري، الزجاج
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari and al-Zajjaj say the number is in the People of the Book’s scripture, confirming Muhammad’s truth because he reported it without reading a book.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬7)، والزجاج (¬8)؛ لأن عدد الخزنة في كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose-lām in “so that they may be certain” attaches to the statement that there are nineteen keepers.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله: {ليستيقن} تتعلق بقوله: {عليها تسعة عشر}

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the number nineteen was already in the scriptures of the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: كان ذلك في كتب أهل الكتاب: تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reads this as certainty added to their existing certainty, since their scripture also gives nineteen keepers.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} يقينا إلى يقينهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this refers to the believers among the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني الذين آمنوا منهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the count was likewise in the People of the Book’s scriptures, so believing scripturalists gain confidence in Muhammad when his report matches theirs.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: لأنهما (¬6) في كتاب أهل الكتاب كذلك

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says believers increase in faith whenever they affirm what comes in God’s Book, including Muhammad’s report of the keepers’ number.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: لأنهم كلما صدقوا بما يأتي في كتاب الله زاد إيمانهم

words: ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that the People of the Book and believers not doubt that Hell’s keepers number nineteen.
rows.anchor: أي لكيلا (¬1) يشك هؤلاء في أن خزنة جهنم تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil identify those with diseased hearts as the doubting hypocrites of Medina.
rows.anchor: أي: شك ونفاق من منافقي المدينة (¬2)، (هذا قول ... (¬3)، والكلبي (¬4)، ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl rejects hypocrisy as the meaning because the sura is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وذكر عن الحسين بن الفضل أنه (¬7) قال: هذه السورة مكية، ولم يكن بمكة نفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defends the exegetes: God knew hypocrisy would arise and foretold what would happen.
rows.anchor: وقول المفسرين صحيح وإن أنكره؛ لأنه كان في معلوم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the disbelievers as the Arab polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني مشركي العرب

rows.speaker: عطاء، الكلبي
rows.claim: Ata and al-Kalbi identify them as Jews and Christians; the author prefers Muqatil because they believe their scripture and would not deny the count.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء (¬1)، (والكلبي (¬2)) (¬3): يعني الكفار من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here mathal means the account itself; unlike 2:26, no parable is explicitly cited, so the disbelievers ask what God intends by this account.
rows.anchor: المثل -هاهنا- الحديث نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the examples from al-Raʿd and al-Fatḥ, mathal also means an account, report, or story.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله: {مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون} [الرعد: 35]، أي: حديثها

words: كذلك يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misleads those who deny the keepers’ number and guides those who affirm and believe it.
rows.anchor: أي كما أضل من أنكر عدد الخزنة، ولم يؤمن به

words: وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement answers Abu Jahl’s claim that Muhammad had only nineteen troops, emphasizing that God’s forces are too numerous to count.
rows.anchor: وأنزل في قول أبي جهل: أما لمحمد من الجنود إلا تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains the reference to God’s troops as emphasizing their vast number.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: أي من الكثرة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says God’s troops are angels created to punish Hell’s inhabitants, whose number only God knows; the nineteen keepers have innumerable angelic auxiliaries.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: "جنود ربك" يعني: من الملائكة الذين خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage returns to mention Saqar as a reminder for humankind.
rows.anchor: ثم رجع إلى ذكر سقر فقال: {وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil gloss it as admonition and reminder for the world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3)، (ومقاتل (¬4)) (¬5)، أي: موعظة وتذكرة للعالم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says the Fire in this world reminds people of the Fire in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: جاء في التفسير أن النار في الدنيا تذكر النار في

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-mustaqarr as the destination: everyone returns to God and every affair ends with Him, as other verses say.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد # المصير

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says that on that day there is no place to depart from it.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول: {إلى ربك يومئذ

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that revelation was difficult to retain, so the Prophet moved his tongue and lips before Gabriel finished, fearing he would forget.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: كان رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- يعالج من التنزيل شدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to move the tongue in recitation while receiving the revelation.
rows.anchor: {لا تحرك به لسانك} يعني بالقراءة (¬4)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To hasten with it means to hasten to receive the Qur’an; the phrasing recalls 20:114.
rows.anchor: كما قال: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه}

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God will gather the Qur’an in the Prophet’s breast and recite it to him.
rows.anchor: قراءته (¬1) عليك؛ (قاله الكلبي)

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata interprets the promise as Gabriel repeating the revelation to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: (أي) (¬4) إن جبريل يستعيده عليك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says this means, “We will recite it to you” until you have memorized it.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل (وقرآنه): يعني: ونقرئكه حتى تحفظه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God will make the Prophet recite it so he does not forget, as in 87:6; on this reading the Prophet recites it, while on the preceding reading Gabriel does.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: إن علينا أن نقرئكه فلا تنسى

rows.speaker: مقاتل، مجاهد، قتادة، عطاء
rows.claim: Muqatil, Mujahid, Qatada, and Ata share this explanation of the command not to move the tongue during revelation.
rows.anchor: هو قول مقاتل (¬8)، (ومجاهد (¬9)، وقتادة (¬10)، وعطاء (¬11))

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses gathering and reciting as preservation; Qur’an connects to gathering, as in the expression that a she-camel had not gathered a fetus.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله: (جمعه وقرآنه) حفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an can mean gathering, as in the expression that a she-camel had not collected a fetus.
rows.anchor: ما قرأت الناقة سلا (¬2) قط، أي: ما جمعت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel is the one reciting when God recites it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فإذا قرأه جبريل (¬5)

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God recites it to the Prophet through Gabriel.
rows.anchor: ومقاتل: فإذا تلوناه عليك بجبريل (¬6)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is to follow what the Qur’an contains as God recites it; Qatada similarly says to follow its lawful and forbidden rulings.
rows.anchor: فاتبع (¬7) قرآنه}. قال: يعني:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says to follow the Qur’an’s lawful and forbidden rulings.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال قتادة: يقول: فاتبع حلاله وحرامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More plausibly, follow its recitation means recite it after Gabriel finishes, since the Prophet was told to stop reading and listen until Gabriel was done.
rows.anchor: وأجود من هذا أن يكون المعنى: فاتبع قرآنه، أي: اقرأه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s report through Said ibn Jubayr, the Prophet listened silently when Gabriel came, then recited after Gabriel left, as promised.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير قال: يقول: إنا أنزلناه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says to listen and be silent when Gabriel comes, then recite after he departs; this follows Gabriel’s recitation by listening.
rows.anchor: وقال (¬5) أيضا: فاتبع قرآنه، واستمع له، وأنصت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ali’s discussion equates the command with the assurance in 20:114 that revelation will be preserved.
rows.anchor: إنا سنحفظه عليك. وهذا في المعنى مثل قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted referent of “it” is the revelation, understood from context, as the omitted referent in 97:1 is understood despite being the sura’s opening.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد بقوله: {جمعه وقرآنه} القرآن الذي هو اسم التنزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the verbal noun refers to the revelation as its object, so it means “our gathering it and our reciting it,” not that the named Qur’an is added to itself.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان الذكر المضاف إليه المصدر في قوله: (وقرآنه) راجعا إلى التنزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same analysis makes the phrase mean “follow our reciting it.”
rows.anchor: وكذلك التقدير في قوله: {فاتبع قرآنه}، ومجاز الآية على قول أبي عبيدة:

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda takes the phrase figuratively as collecting and arranging the parts; the camel expression and Amr ibn Kulthum’s line use qaraʾa for gathering or carrying a fetus.
rows.anchor: مجاز الآية على قول أبي عبيدة: جمعه وتأليف بعضه إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing general gathering with the more specific Qur’an or recitation is apt repetition, like gathering people or wealth, where one would not say “read the people.”
rows.anchor: وإنما حسن ذكر الجمع والقرآن؛ لأن المجى عام، والقرآن أخص منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second term adding a meaning absent from the first is especially apt, as when “inform” is paired with “warn.”
rows.anchor: كما أنك لو قلت: أعلمت زيدا وأنذرته، حسن؛ لاختصاص الإنذار بمعنى التخويف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، المفسرون
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes identify the person as Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2) والمفسرون (¬3): يعني: أبو جهل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Abu Jahl did not believe in the Messenger’s mission and did not submit.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: يقول: لم [يصدق] (¬4) أبو جهل بالرسالة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Abu Jahl did not believe in the Qur’an and did not pray to God.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: [لم يصدق] (¬6) بالقرآن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة، المبرد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Mubarrad read the phrase as not believing or praying; lā can negate the past as well as the future, as in 90:11, a hadith, and Tarafa’s line.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة (¬8)، والمبرد (¬9): أي لم يصدق، ولم يصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denied the Qur’an, turned away from faith, and returned to his family.
rows.anchor: قوله: {ولكن كذب}، أي: بالقرآن. {وتولى} عن الإيمان.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، المفسرون
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes explain yatematta as swaggering and walking arrogantly.
rows.anchor: يتبختر ويختال في مشيته، (قاله ابن عباس (¬3)

rows.speaker: مقاتل، زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Muqatil and Zayd ibn Aslam call it the characteristic gait of Banu Makhzum.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل (¬6)، وزيد بن أسلم (¬7): هو مشية بني مخزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation is from maṭw, stretching; the report says Abu Bakr passed Bilal stretching in the sun, and yatematta means to stretch oneself.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه (من المطو، وهو المد.

rows.speaker: الفراء، الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj derive it from al-maṭā, the back: he twists his back in an arrogant gait.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء (¬3)، والزجاج (¬4): هو من المطا، وهو الظهر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة، ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and Ibn Qutayba derive it from al-maṭṭ, stretching; Ibn Qutayba explains a consonant shift from yatematta.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عبيدة (¬7)، وابن قتيبة (¬8) في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says this sura and its verses were revealed in installments, unlike other scriptures; Muqatil agrees.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: السورة، والآية، والآيتين لم تنزل جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Them” refers to the Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: {ولا تطع منهم} يعني: من مشركي مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinful person is Utba ibn Rabiʿa, who asked the Prophet to abandon his mission and offered to marry him to one of his children.
rows.anchor: آثما} يعني: عتبة بن ربيعة، قال للنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

rows.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
rows.claim: The ungrateful person is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who offered wealth until the Prophet was satisfied and boasted of his riches.
rows.anchor: قاله الكلبي (¬7)، ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says aw here functions like lā, supported by a verse where it means “nor”; it can also approach wāw and encompass either case.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: (أو) هاهنا بمنزلة (لا)، وأنشد (¬10)، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farra’s example means “I will give you whether you ask or remain silent,” illustrating aw close to wāw in the sense of “in any case.”
rows.anchor: كقولك للرجل: لأعطينك سألت، أو سكت، معناه: لأعطينك على كل حال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Abu Jahl threatened to step on Muhammad’s neck if he saw him praying, prompting this command.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يتجه قول قتادة: إن أبا جهل قال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says aw is stronger than wāw because it makes each person individually someone not to obey; he compares Zayd and Amr with al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: (أو) هاهنا أوكد من (الواو)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse parallels the account that God made human offspring from an extract of lowly water in 32:8, also discussed in Surat al-Muʾminun.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين (8)}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known appointed term is the duration of pregnancy and its endpoint.
rows.anchor: {إلى قدر معلوم (22)} يعني مدة الحامل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God fashioned the child’s traits, including height or shortness and whether male or female.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني خلقه، كيف يكون قصيرا، وطويلا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The light and doubled readings have the same meaning; Arab usage allows both, so the argument from 77:23 for the light reading is not decisive.
rows.anchor: وفيه قراءتان: التخفيف، والتشديد (¬4). قال الفراء: والمعنى فيهما واحد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali allows the doubled form to mean “the estimators,” with extra letters dropped as in the cited Arabic forms; he refers to 15:22.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: ويجوز أن يكون:

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari defines a mirṣād as a place where a watcher waits for an enemy, like the place where horses are trained.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: المرصاد: المكان الذي يرصد الراصد فيه العدو

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls it a place for watching, meaning Hell is prepared for its occupants.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: مرصادا محلا يرصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is a station from which its keepers watch the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وجهنم مرصاد يرصد به خزنتها الكفار

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق، الحسن
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says Hell watches unbelievers and those due for punishment; al-Hasan says, by God, it watches them.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: يرصد أهل الكفر، ومن حق عليه العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirṣād may be an intensive pattern from raṣada, denoting constant watchfulness, like miʿṭār and miʿmār.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يجوز أن يكون المرصاد مفعالا من الرصد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify the transgressors as misguided polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5)، ومقاتل (¬6): يريد للمشركين الضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To purify oneself means to become free of associating partners with God, as in 91:9 and the description in 18:74.
rows.anchor: أي تتطهر من الشرك، ومنه قوله: {قد أفلح من زكاها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits a required noun; the sense is, “Do you have a need or desire for that?”
rows.anchor: والمبتدأ محذوف [في] (¬6) اللفظ مراد في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed line about having a need for someone illustrates the elliptical construction and implied desire.
rows.anchor: فهل لكم فيها إلي فإنني ... بصير بما أعيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled reading assimilates the verb’s tāʾ into zāy; the light reading drops the tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وفيه قراءتان: التشديد (¬1) على إدغام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets becoming purified as testifying that there is no deity but God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله:

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses it as affirming God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: توحد الله

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets it as doing good.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: تعمل خيرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say Moses offers to call Pharaoh to worship his Lord.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬8)، ومقاتل (¬9): وأدعوك إلى عبادة ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gloss says Pharaoh would be saved through fear of God and affirm God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: {فتخشى} فتسلم من خشية الله، وتوحد الله

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning say it is fear of God’s punishment, fulfilled by carrying out the duties imposed out of that fear.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: فتخشى عقابه، ويكون المعنى: تؤدي ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turned away from truth and faith and set about spreading corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن الحق، والإيمان (¬7). {يسعى} يعمل بالفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gathered his people and soldiers, then called out.
rows.anchor: وهو قوله تعالى: {فحشر فنادى} فجمع قومه، وجنوده فنادى

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق، المبرد
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq treats nakāl as an emphatic verbal noun: taking Pharaoh means punishing him; al-Mubarrad agrees, as in 11:102.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: "نكال" مصدر مؤكدة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra paraphrases it as God seizing him with exemplary punishment for this life and the next.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: يريد أخذه الله أخذا نكالا للآخرة والأولى

rows.speaker: مجاهد، الشعبي، سعيد بن جبير، مقاتل، عطاء والكلبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view takes the two terms as Pharaoh’s claims, “I know no god for you but me” and later “I am your highest lord,” forty years apart.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول (مجاهد (¬2)، والشعبي (¬3)، وسعيد بن جبير (¬4)، ومقاتل (¬5)

rows.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Pharaoh was drowned and punished in this world, then punished in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬8)، # وقتادة (¬1):

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who transgresses and prefers worldly life is a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {فأما من طغى (37) وآثر الحياة الدنيا} يعني الكافر

rows.speaker: مقاتل، الكلبي
rows.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say the verses were revealed about al-Nadr and his father al-Harith.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬5)، والكلبي (¬6): نزلت في النضر وأبيه الحرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʾwā is the place that shelters or receives him.
rows.anchor: أي المأوى (¬7) تأويه)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Hell is the abode of whoever has this description.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي هي: المأوى) (¬9) لمن كان

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the person seeks independence from faith.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: يريد عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say he considers himself independent of God; the word is also glossed as being wealthy.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي (¬3)، ومقاتل (¬4): استغنى عن الله في نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads “may the human be cursed” as a curse upon Utba.
rows.anchor: هو قال ابن عباس: لعن عتبة (¬6)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say the verse was revealed about Utba ibn Abi Lahab.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: نزلت في (عتبة بن) (¬7) أبي لهب

rows.speaker: مقاتل، الكلبي
rows.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi gloss the question as “What made him disbelieve?”
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬9)، الكلبي (¬10): ما الذي أكفره

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says this is the established exegetical reading, while allowing an exclamative construction.
rows.anchor: وقال (¬11) الفراء: بهذا الوجه جاء التفسير

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives two construals: an exclamation inviting people to marvel at human disbelief, like 2:175, or a rebuking question, “What made him disbelieve?”
rows.anchor: وشرح الزجاج القولين، فقال: يكون على جهة لفظ التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased as a question, it is a reminder affirming that God created the human and that He is one.
rows.anchor: {من أي شيء خلقه} لفظه استفهام، ومعناه التقرير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say God determines the child in its mother’s womb.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬7)، # ومقاتل (¬1):

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says God shapes the human through stages from sperm to clot and onward, determining sex and whether the person is fortunate or wretched.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره الفراء: وقدره أطوارا: نطفة، علقة إلى آخر خلقه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads it as proportioning the human into an upright form, comparing 18:37.
rows.anchor: والثاني: ما ذكره الزجاج قال: المعنى: فقدره على الاستواء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God proportioned the body’s form, head, eyes, hands, and feet.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكلبي: (قدر خلقه، ورأسه، وعينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is directed to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: {يا أيها الإنسان} (¬9)، مخاطبة للكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what deceived the human and enticed him into falsehood until he neglected what was due to God.
rows.anchor: (أي ما خدعك، وسول إليك الباطل حتى أضعت ما وجب عليك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also asks who made him feel safe from punishment; the idiom means giving someone false assurance against a danger from an unreliable source, as in 35:5.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: ما الذي أمنك من عقابه، ويقال: غره بفلان، إذا أمنه

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: قال (عطاء عن) (¬1) ابن عباس: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says it was revealed about Abu al-Ashaddayn Kalda ibn Asid, who struck the Prophet but was not punished, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: نزلت في أبي الأشدين كلدة بن أسيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the enemy set over the human, Satan, deceived him.
rows.anchor: فقال قتادة: غره العدو المسلط عليه، يعني الشيطان

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym says ignorance deceived him; the report is transmitted as raised to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: غره الجهل (¬7)، وهو يروى مرفوعا (¬8)

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God’s forbearance deceived him, since He did not punish him immediately.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: غره عفو الله عنه حين لم يعاقبه في أول أمره
